title: Charges and masses of subatomic particles
keyIdea: Protons (+1, mass 1) and neutrons (0, mass 1) sit in the tiny nucleus; electrons (−1, mass almost 0) are outside it.

kid: An atom has a tiny nucleus in the middle. It holds protons and neutrons. Electrons move around the outside in shells.
A proton has a charge of +1. An electron has a charge of −1. A neutron has no charge. Protons and neutrons each have a mass of 1. An electron is so light that we say its mass is almost 0.
adult: Relative charges: proton +1, neutron 0, electron −1. Relative masses: proton 1, neutron 1, electron about 1/1840.
Atoms are neutral because they have equal numbers of protons and electrons. Mass number = protons + neutrons. An ion forms when an atom gains or loses electrons: lose one and the charge is +1.

familyTip: Make a table with three rows (proton, neutron, electron) and two columns (charge, mass). Cover it and test each other.
